label: Claude Sonnet 5.5
output:
To: Shared/Ops & HR
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: Monday at Embakasi: casuals' pay, what to say and what not to say

Brian,

You asked for something you can read on Sunday without guessing. This is it. I'm up from 4:30 on Monday and my flight leaves at 7:05, so message me before I board if anything changes. After that I'm in the air and can't help live, which is why I've tried to cover the hard parts below.

The one thing to hold on to: this is our mess, not theirs. The guys did their work and should have been paid on Friday. Don't walk in defensive. Walk in owing them an apology, because we do.

WHAT ACTUALLY HAPPENED

The fortnight's casual payroll (212 people) went to the bank on Friday as a bulk payment file. The bank rejected the whole file at validation. They upgraded their platform on 25 November and now require a new file template, and one column in ours was too long. Nothing was processed, so nobody was short-paid and no money went to the wrong place.

The rejection notice went to an old finance mailbox, so finance only saw it after 5pm on Friday, after the bank's cut-off. By then there was nothing anyone could do until Monday. That's two failures on our side: a file in the wrong format, and an alert nobody saw in time.

When you explain it to the guys, keep it short and honest: the bank rejected our file because of a format problem on our side, we only found out after the bank had closed, and that's the company's fault. Don't name Kevin or finance to the crowd. Don't go into the mailbox detail either. If anyone asks questions you can't answer, say you'll find out and come back to them, and then do it.

WHEN THE MONEY LANDS

We're not waiting for the bank. Njeri approved paying everyone through an M-Pesa bulk payment instead. Kevin's realistic estimate is money on phones by 11am on Monday. He would not promise earlier, and I won't either.

That estimate is the only time we have. Please remember Mombasa in 2024: the supervisor told the casuals "by lunch", the money came at 4pm, and half the shift sat down. We never give a time we can't keep.

So here's what I'd do:

1. Call Kevin on Sunday evening. Ask him to confirm the batch is ready to go first thing and to text you the moment it's submitted. Then you can tell the guys it has been sent, not that it's on its way.
2. Only say "11am" to the guys if Kevin has confirmed it to you. If he hasn't, say "today, and I'll stand here at 11 and tell you exactly where it is". A time you'll show up at is safer than a time the money has to hit.
3. If it lands earlier, good. Let it be a pleasant surprise.

Rent is due on the 1st, which is Tuesday. Money on Monday means everyone has it before then. Say that plainly. Joseph tells me several of them are worried about it.

THE 14 NUMBERS

Peninah has checked the list. 198 numbers are confirmed. 14 she couldn't reach, mostly the new loaders from the Athi River intake. Those 14 have to give her a correct number before they can be paid.

She'll be at Embakasi from 7:30 with a printout and her laptop. Anyone who wants a payslip printed can get one from her. Tell everyone about this at the start so the 14 know to go to her first thing, and so nobody thinks they've been left off.

Don't promise those 14 the same 11am time as everyone else. Ask Peninah and Kevin on Sunday how quickly a corrected number can be paid after she has it, and promise only what they tell you. Do tell the 14 that the delay is a phone number problem, not a pay problem, and that they're in the same batch of arrangements as everyone else.

WHAT YOU CAN PROMISE

- Everyone on the affected list gets paid by M-Pesa, Monday, with the time as above.
- Each person on the affected list also gets KES 500 for Monday lunch and fare, in the same M-Pesa batch. Njeri approved this.
- The M-Pesa charges are on the company. Nothing is deducted from anyone's pay for them. If someone asks about the fee at the agent when they cash out, don't promise anything. Say you'll check with Kevin.
- A proper apology from management, in person. Njeri asked for it specifically and asked you to give it because I'm travelling. Say it to the whole group yourself, in your own words. Something like: "This was our mistake. You did your work and you should have been paid Friday. I'm sorry. Here is what's happening and when."

WHAT YOU MUST NOT PROMISE

- Any time earlier than what Kevin has confirmed.
- Any "tomorrow" or "by lunch" you can't back up. They told Joseph that the last time management said "tomorrow", it took three days. That's what you're up against.
- Anything about rent, advances, loans or paying landlords. We haven't approved any of it and you shouldn't improvise it.
- Anything beyond the KES 500 and the M-Pesa charges. If someone asks for more, say you'll take it to me and Njeri.
- Don't guess at reasons beyond what's written above. Stick to the bank file and the late alert.
- No mention of contracts, dismissal, replacement workers or "people who don't want to work". Our own procedure forbids threatening anyone with dismissal on the day, and it would also be the fastest way to turn a bad morning into a bad week.

IF OUMA'S GROUP WON'T LOAD THE KISUMU TRUCKS

Joseph says Ouma and two others are telling people not to load until they see money. The Kisumu trucks have to leave by 9 to make the offloading slot at the mill. Ouma is loud, but he isn't a bad man. He has four kids and rent to pay, and he's reacting to being let down. Treat him that way.

Rough plan for the morning:

- 5:30: you arrive. Spend a few minutes with Joseph first. Find out who is saying what and who has already turned up.
- Before the shift starts: find Ouma and talk to him privately, before you speak to the whole group. Don't ambush him in front of people. Tell him what you'd tell the rest: it was our mistake, here's what happened, here's when the money comes, and I'd like you to hear it from me first. Listen to him properly before you ask for anything. If he feels heard, half of this goes away.
- Then speak to the whole group at the start of the shift. Apologise first, give the facts, and say what you can promise, then stop. Don't turn it into a debate.
- Peninah arrives at 7:30 for the 14 numbers. Point people to her.

What to ask of Ouma: that his group load the Kisumu trucks while the money is on its way. Be straight that you can't make the money arrive before it does. What you can do is promise to stand in front of them at 11 and tell them exactly where it is. If Kevin has texted you that the batch is submitted, show him that.

If they still won't load:

- Don't argue and don't threaten. A refusal to work isn't a grievance channel under our procedure, but it also isn't something you handle by pressure. Any stoppage is handled by Operations and HR together, and nobody is to be dismissed or threatened with dismissal on the day.
- Work backwards from 9am. You know the loading time better than I do. Decide now what is the latest the loading can start and still get the trucks away.
- Call the mill by about 7:30 to ask whether a later offloading slot is possible. Don't wait until 9 to find out. This might come to nothing, but it's much better to have asked early.
- Don't bring in outside loaders at the gate. It will look like punishment, and it will harden the group.
- Bring in HR. Until I board, call or WhatsApp me. Once I'm in the air, call Njeri. She has already asked for the apology, so she knows the situation and can be the management half of the joint decision. Note down who decided what and when.
- A late truck is a problem we can fix with the mill. A walkout that spreads to the rest of the shift is much harder to fix.

AFTER MONDAY

If the money has landed and things have calmed down, a short word to Ouma afterwards will help. Thank him for hearing you out. Any grievances beyond this go to Joseph first and then to HR within 48 hours, per the procedure. When I'm back on Wednesday evening I'll follow up with you and Kevin on the template and the mailbox so this can't happen again, and I'll want to hear how it went.

SUNDAY CHECKLIST

1. Call Kevin: confirm the 11am estimate, ask him to text when the batch is submitted, and ask about the 14.
2. Check with Peninah that she's set for 7:30 and knows how the 14 will be paid.
3. Ask Joseph who is with Ouma and who is likely to follow him.
4. Work out the latest time loading can start for the 9am departure, and have the mill's number ready.
5. Keep my number and Njeri's handy.

You've handled worse than this, and the guys know you. Go in honest, say sorry first, and promise only what we can keep.

Achieng
